hook: What if an Arizona volcano dwarfed Mount St. Helens 1,000 times?

sections.voiceover: What if an Arizona volcano dwarfed Mount St. Helens 1,000 times?
b_roll: Volcanic landscape vector motion graphic showing massive ash eruption

sections.voiceover: Where did all those volcanic ash deposits from Turkey Creek Volcano actually end up?
b_roll: Map animation of southeastern Arizona highlighting Turkey Creek Volcano
Animation of cooling rhyolite tuff rock layers

sections.voiceover: But erosion slowly carved those ash layers into stone towers at Chiricahua National Park.
b_roll: Graphic transition to Chiricahua National Park rock pinnacles

sections.voiceover: The volcano released 1,000 times more material than Mount St. Helens. In the 1930s, the Civilian Conservation Corps named rhyolite formations along Ed Riggs Trail.
b_roll: Bar chart comparing volcanic material volume versus Mount St. Helens
Historical map graphic showing Civilian Conservation Corps and Ed Riggs Trail

sections.voiceover: Today, those 27 million year old rocks still stand.
b_roll: Cinematic graphics of rhyolite standing rocks
